dedupe_keys.name: epa excess food opportunities map version 3 1

description: The Excess Food Opportunities Map shows where surplus food is generated in the United States and where it could go instead of landfill. The US Environmental Protection Agency built it to support nationwide diversion of excess food. It maps more than 960,000 potential generators in the industrial, commercial and institutional sectors, such as food manufacturers and processors, wholesalers, supermarkets, restaurants, hospitals, schools and correctional facilities, with estimates of excess food by generator type, and more than 15,000 potential recipients, including food banks, pantries and soup kitchens, composting sites and anaerobic digestion facilities, plus communities with separate organics collection and refrigerated warehouses. Version 3.1 updated food bank, farmers market, composting and anaerobic digestion layers after the full 3.0 refresh of July 2023. The map is free to use and its data can be downloaded as a US government product. Caveats: EPA states that locations are for information only and have not been verified, and generator quantities are modelled estimates, not measured tonnages. Simulation uses: modelling food rescue and redistribution networks after a disruption, siting organics processing capacity, and locating food banks and cold storage exposed to hazards for emergency food supply planning. Related records: Feeding America's Map the Meal Gap (data-feeding-america-map-the-meal-gap) describes demand for food assistance, and the EPA Recycling Infrastructure and Market Opportunities Map (data-epa-recycling-infrastructure-market-opportunities-map) covers other recycling plants.
